title: Subitising
examples: Can we practice with more dots?
How do I know how many dots are there?

explain.say: Look at these dots. Say how many you see, straight away.
You can see a small group and know how many at once. This is called subitising. You see the whole group, without counting each dot.

draw.text: Subitising: seeing how many at once

explain.say: Dice show the same dot patterns every time. Two dots sit on a line. Five dots are two, one and two.
A ten-frame has two rows of five boxes. Here four boxes have a dot. You can see four, straight away.
Start with groups of up to five. When that feels easy, try up to ten.

faq.a: Subitising means you see a small group and know how many, without counting. It is a quick number skill.
asks: How do I know how many dots are there?

faq.q: Do I have to count every time?
faq.a: No. With a small group, you can see the number straight away. You count when the group is bigger.
asks: Can I just guess the number?
Is it okay if I count sometimes?

faq.q: How does the ten-frame help me?
faq.a: A ten-frame has two rows of five boxes. A full row is five, and a full frame is ten. This helps you see numbers up to ten.
asks: Why do we use the ten-frame?

faq.q: Can I use my fingers to help?
faq.a: Yes. Fingers are a good way to practise. Hold up three fingers and see three at once.
asks: Is it okay to count on my fingers?

faq.q: Is this for big numbers only?
faq.a: No. You start with small groups, up to five. Then you build up to ten.
asks: Will I learn big numbers next?
Do I have to learn this for big numbers?

facts: Subitising is seeing a small group of items and knowing the total.
It is a quick way to know the number without counting each one.
Dice are often used to practise subitising.
The ten-frame helps you see numbers up to ten.

quiz.say: Look at the dots. Tap how many.
quiz.why: There are three dots. You can see three at once.

wrong.1: Look again, because there is one more dot.
wrong.2: Look again, because there is one dot less than that.

quiz.say: Look at the dice. Tap how many dots.
quiz.why: There are five dots. Dice show five as two, one and two.

wrong.0: Look at the middle, because there is one more dot there.
wrong.1: Six on a dice is two rows of three dots.

quiz.say: Look at the ten-frame. Tap how many dots.
quiz.why: Four boxes have a dot. That is one less than a full row of five.

wrong.0: Ten is all the boxes, but just some boxes have dots.
wrong.2: A full row is five, and this row has one empty box.
